Subject: Draft MSA + Order Form: DPA redline (first pass)

Marcus — thanks for the demo last week. Attached is our first-pass redline to the DPA tied to the MSA/order form you shared. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm whether Redwood can accept the standard SCCs (EU Commission 2021) as-is or if you require your own controller-processor mapping exhibit.
- We need clarity on processor role assignment for embeddings/analytics pipelines (are they controller-facing features or processor-only operations?).
- Please provide a short evidence manifest for export controls and KMS locality for EU data (CSV preferable).

We've annotated the redline with comments (see attachment). Can you coordinate legal ops and come back with a consolidated response and a proposed workback for evidence delivery? We have an internal procurement review on Oct 20 and would like to close order form redlines before then.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Grant
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
NovaBio Therapeutics

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@novabio.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form: DPA redline (first pass)

Sophie — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (privacy counsel) and Ben (sales lead) to coordinate legal and evidence. Quick answers up-front:

- SCCs: We can accept the EU Commission 2021 SCCs but will need to add an exhibit that maps the roles and subprocessors used for embeddings and analytics; that exhibit is a short table, not a legal rewrite.
- Roles: Embeddings + analytics are "processor operations" under the MSA; however, if NovaBio supplies labeled training data for model updates, that triggers controller-controller discussions (we won't do training without a separate agreement).
- Evidence manifest: we'll produce a CSV listing KMS region, subprocessor host regions, and export-control flags — target delivery Oct 15.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Kimberly — review and comment on the redline, prioritize the SCCs exhibit and the KMS locality language.
2) Ben — verify procurement timeline and whether procurement needs an SKAdNetwork-style SLA exception or a letters-of-scope certificate.
3) Laura — pull subprocessor list and start the CSV stub (I'll share a template).

I'll compile a single response for you by Oct 8.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form: DPA redline (first pass)

Marcus / team — quick legal ops notes after an initial pass on Sophie's redline:

1) SCCs: Acceptable; we will attach the standard 2021 SCCs and add a short exhibit (Annex E) that enumerates controller/processor roles for the top-level services (generation, embeddings, analytics). Draft language: "Annex E: Role allocation and subprocessor roster — non-exhaustive; subject to updates via the console." This keeps us from having to renegotiate core clauses.

2) Liability/Indemnity: NovaBio redlined a cap carveout for data breaches involving healthcare data. We should push for a waiver limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct in the exhibit; otherwise keep the standard MSA cap.

3) Data transfers: we will propose a transfer-impact addendum that includes: (a) controller/processor mapping, (b) list of subprocessors and KMS regions, (c) export-control flags. This will be a 1-2 page addendum, not an annexed TIA document.

4) Evidence delivery: Laura — can you produce the CSV with columns: subprocessor, host_region, KMS_region, export_control_flag, last_audit_date. Aim for Oct 13 delivery so Kimberly can sign off by Oct 14.

5) DocuSign and execution path: If NovaBio confirms material terms, we can run the final MSA+Order Form through standard e-sign (no external countersign needed unless they request additional countersigns).

I'll prepare draft exhibit language by Oct 9 and circulate. Short and surgical is the goal — avoid reauthoring the SCCs themselves.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_notes_sophies_redline.txt

Marcus — appreciate the quick turnaround and Kimberly's helpful summary. Two quick clarifications before we lock the workback:

- Can the Annex E exhibit remain editable (one-way from Redwood) so that changes to subprocessor roster are published through the console and considered "notified"? We prefer that cadence rather than document amendments.
- For the evidence CSV, procurement wants a signed one-pager certifying "no export controlled data flows to sanctioned destinations". Is there a standard Redwood statement we can reference?

If you can confirm those two items, we'll push procurement to the Oct 20 window. Otherwise procurement may ask for a two-week buffer.

Sophie and I are available for a quick 20-min call tomorrow (Mon) to triage.

Thanks — Tom
